statement: A slot whose hours exceed 23 or whose minutes exceed 59 is rejected with InvalidTimeError.

faults.description: Minute limit loosened to 60, so a start minute of 60 passes the time check and is reported as a different error.
The time-range check is removed, so 24:00-25:00 is no longer rejected with InvalidTimeError.

statement: A slot must start and end on a quarter hour and last at least 15 minutes, otherwise it is rejected with InvalidRangeError.

faults.description: The end-on-quarter-hour check is disabled, so 10:00-10:20 is accepted.
The minimum duration is raised to 30 minutes, so a valid 15-minute slot such as 10:00-10:15 is rejected.

statement: Two slots conflict only when they overlap for at least one minute, and slots that merely touch do not conflict.

faults.description: The comparison becomes inclusive, so touching slots 09:00-10:00 and 10:00-11:00 are reported as conflicting.
The second bound compares b.start to b.end instead of a.end, so any slot that starts before b ends is treated as a conflict, including disjoint later ones.

statement: Free gaps between 08:00 and 20:00 are returned in ascending order after merging overlapping or touching bookings, including the trailing gap up to 20:00.

faults.description: The cursor is set to the booking end instead of the furthest end seen, so a booking nested inside an earlier longer one reopens an already-booked period as a gap.
The trailing gap up to 20:00 is never emitted, so no bookings yields no gap instead of 08:00-20:00.

statement: Members and drop-in visitors pay their specified off-peak and peak hourly rates, and an unrecognized customer type is rejected with UnknownCustomerError.

faults.description: The drop-in peak rate is raised to 6500 cents per hour, which changes the price only for drop-in visitors in peak hours.
The unknown-customer guard is removed, so an unrecognized type fails with a TypeError instead of UnknownCustomerError.

statement: A slot's price is its off-peak minutes at the off-peak rate plus its peak minutes at the peak rate, each prorated per minute.

faults.description: The peak window start is no longer applied, so a slot like 10:30-11:00 counts every minute from 10:00 to its end as peak.
The off-peak and peak rates are swapped, so off-peak minutes are charged at the peak rate and vice versa.

statement: Money formatting renders whole cents as a dollar sign, dollars with thousands separators, a period and exactly two cent digits.

faults.description: The thousands separator is replaced with an empty string, so 123456 renders as $1234.56 instead of $1,234.56.
The cents are no longer zero-padded, so 5 renders as $0.5 instead of $0.05.

statement: A slot summary is a single line holding the slot text, its formatted duration in parentheses, and the formatted price.

faults.description: Whole-hour durations lose their hour part (the hour is only shown above 1), so a 60-minute slot summarizes as (0m) instead of (1h).
The duration is computed from the end minute instead of end minus start, so the displayed duration is wrong.
The parenthesized duration is dropped from the summary line.
